proposals.before: When Zhao Sixian rose in rebellion at Yongxing, Emperor Yindi of Later Han ordered Guo Congyi to crush him and appointed Jun director of armies and cavalry.
proposals.after: When Zhao Siwan rose in rebellion at Yongxing, Emperor Yindi of Later Han ordered Guo Congyi to crush him and appointed Jun director of armies and cavalry.
proposals.reason: 趙思綰 is Siwan (思綰), not Sixian; the idiomatic spelling misreads the given name.

proposals.before: When Guo Wei marched north and reached Cangzhou, the armies pressed him to take the throne. Jun and Wang Yin, hearing the news in the capital, dispatched Palace Guard cavalry commander Guo Chong to Songzhou and the former prefect of Shen, Ma Duo, to Xuzhou to forestall any other upheaval. Both prefectures stayed calm—another stroke planned by Jun.
proposals.after: When Guo Wei marched north and reached Chanzhou, the armies pressed him to take the throne. Jun and Wang Yin, hearing the news in the capital, dispatched Palace Guard cavalry commander Guo Chong to Songzhou and the former prefect of Shen, Ma Duo, to Xuzhou (Xu Prefecture) to forestall any other upheaval. Both prefectures stayed calm—another stroke planned by Jun.
proposals.reason: 澶州 is Chanzhou (near Puyang), not Cangzhou (滄州); the idiomatic place-name is wrong.

proposals.before: Taizu marched north, reached Cangzhou, was pressed by the armies; Jun and Wang Yin in the capital heard the change, then sent Palace Guard cavalry commander Guo Chong to Songzhou, former Shen prefect Ma Duo to Xuzhou, to guard against other changes; the two prefectures were secure—also Jun's plan.
proposals.after: Taizu marched north, reached Chanzhou, was pressed by the armies; Jun and Wang Yin in the capital heard the change, then sent Palace Guard cavalry commander Guo Chong to Songzhou, former Shen prefect Ma Duo to Xuzhou, to guard against other changes; the two prefectures were secure—also Jun's plan.
proposals.reason: Literal likewise renders 澶州 as Cangzhou; it should be Chanzhou.

proposals.before: Soon afterward Shizong came from Cazhou to attend court. Jun had long feared his intelligence and resolve; hearing that he was on his way to the capital, Jun left the river works at once and returned.
proposals.after: Soon afterward Shizong came from Chanzhou to attend court. Jun had long feared his intelligence and resolve; hearing that he was on his way to the capital, Jun left the river works at once and returned.
proposals.reason: 澶州 is Chanzhou, not Cazhou.

proposals.before: Before long Shizong came from Cazhou to present himself at court. Jun had always feared Shizong's intelligence and martial resolve; hearing that he was proceeding to the capital, he at once returned to court from his post on the river.
proposals.after: Before long Shizong came from Chanzhou to present himself at court. Jun had always feared Shizong's intelligence and martial resolve; hearing that he was proceeding to the capital, he at once returned to court from his post on the river.
proposals.reason: Literal likewise misrenders 澶州 as Cazhou.

proposals.before: Under the Zhou founder, Yanchao submitted a letter purportedly from Gao Xingzhou, military governor of Yan Prefecture, whose wording suggested that Xingzhou had slandered the emperor and was conspiring with Yanchao. Guo Wei read it and laughed: "This must be Yanchao's trick."
proposals.after: Under the Zhou founder, Yanchao submitted a letter purportedly from Gao Xingzhou, military governor of Yun Prefecture, whose wording suggested that Xingzhou had slandered the emperor and was conspiring with Yanchao. Guo Wei read it and laughed: "This must be Yanchao's trick."
proposals.reason: 鄆州 is Yun Prefecture, not Yan Prefecture (兗州); the idiomatic confuses the two.

proposals.before: The genuine Yanzhou seal had a flaw where the characters did not meet; the forged seal had no such gap. The emperor soon sent the letter to Xingzhou to show him the truth, and Xingzhou memorialized his thanks.
proposals.after: The genuine Yunzhou seal had a flaw where the characters did not meet; the forged seal had no such gap. The emperor soon sent the letter to Xingzhou to show him the truth, and Xingzhou memorialized his thanks.
proposals.reason: Continues the 鄆州→Yanzhou error; it should be Yunzhou.

decisions.reason: Focus unit names 趙思綰; 綰 is wan, so the given name is Siwan, not Sixian. The proposed personal-name fix is accurate and leaves the rest of the sentence unchanged.

decisions.after: When Guo Wei marched north and reached Chanzhou, the armies pressed him to take the throne. Jun and Wang Yin, hearing the news in the capital, dispatched Palace Guard cavalry commander Guo Chong to Songzhou and the former prefect of Shen, Ma Duo, to Xuzhou to forestall any other upheaval. Both prefectures stayed calm—another stroke planned by Jun.
decisions.reason: 澶州 is Chanzhou, not Cangzhou (滄州), so that place-name must be corrected; the added parenthetical “(Xu Prefecture)” after the already adequate Xuzhou for 許州 is an unnecessary stylistic gloss and is dropped.
The literal likewise misreads 澶州 as Cangzhou; replacing it with Chanzhou restores the correct place-name without other changes.
Focus unit has 自澶州; Cazhou is a garbled romanization of 澶州, and Chanzhou is the correct place-name.
The literal repeats the same 澶州→Cazhou error; Chanzhou is the accurate replacement.
Focus unit names 鄆州節度使, which is Yun Prefecture, not Yan Prefecture (兗州). The proposed office place-name fix is correct.
Focus unit continues with 鄆州印; Yanzhou wrongly equates it with 兗州, and Yunzhou correctly names the Yun seal.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0001 shows English Zhao Sixian was produced only by misreading 思綰; the personal-name claim must use Zhao Siwan while keeping zh and the claim identity fields.
Accepted r0001 shows the given-name claim Sixian came only from the bad idiomatic; 綰 is wan, so the English and pinyin must be Siwan.
